rules.title: California Civil Code section 1946.2 (Tenant Protection Act of 2019 – just cause)
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a unit for 12 months, the owner may not terminate the tenancy without stating a just cause (at-fault or no-fault) in the written notice. For no-fault terminations the owner must pay one month's rent as relocation assistance (within 15 days of notice) or waive the final month's rent.
rules.key_value: 12 months occupancy; relocation assistance equal to one month's rent
rules.penalty: Non-compliant notice is void; owner liable for actual damages, attorney's fees, and up to three times actual damages (plus punitive damages) for willful or malicious violations; injunctive relief by Attorney General, city attorney or county counsel.
rules.status_basis: Document references July 1, 2020 and January 1, 2020 dates for lease provisions, but does not state the section's own enactment or effective date.

requires.name: residential_tenancy_12_months
requires.text: after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months

exempt_if.text: Housing that has been issued a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years, unless the housing is a mobilehome.

exempt_if.name: institutional_housing
exempt_if.text: Nonprofit hospital, religious facility, extended care facility, residential care facility for the elderly, adult residential facility; dormitories owned and operated by higher education or K-12 school

exempt_if.name: shared_facilities_with_owner
exempt_if.text: Tenant shares bathroom or kitchen facilities with the owner who maintains their principal residence at the property

exempt_if.name: owner_occupied_single_family
exempt_if.text: Single-family owner-occupied residences renting no more than two units or bedrooms, or a mobilehome

exempt_if.name: owner_occupied_duplex
exempt_if.text: Two dwelling units in a single structure where the owner occupied one as principal residence at start of tenancy and neither is an ADU or JADU

exempt_if.name: separately_alienable_non_corporate_owner
exempt_if.text: Residential property alienable separate from title to any other dwelling unit where the owner is not a REIT, corporation, or LLC with a corporate member, and the required exemption notice was given

exempt_if.name: affordable_housing
exempt_if.text: Housing restricted by deed or agreement as affordable for very low, low, or moderate income persons, or subject to housing subsidies agreement

exempt_if.name: stricter_local_just_cause_ordinance
exempt_if.text: Property subject to a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or a more protective one adopted or amended after that date

coverage.summary: Applies to residential tenancies of 12 months or more (24 months if adult tenants were added to the lease) statewide.
coverage.exemptions_summary: Exempts recently built housing (certificate of occupancy within 15 years), hotels, institutional housing, owner-shared or owner-occupied small properties, qualifying non-corporate-owned single-unit properties, affordable housing, and properties covered by local just cause ordinances.

precedence.text: Does not apply to property subject to a local just cause ordinance adopted on or before September 1, 2019, or adopted or amended after that date that is more protective; a less protective later local ordinance is not enforced.

rules.quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
